llm.why_not_core: 论文仅通过模拟研究孔隙率，未提供任何力学性能（如拉伸、疲劳）的实验或计算数据。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of paving speed on porosity formation in Ti-6Al-4V alloy during laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: A process simulation approach is employed to model the influence of paving speed on porosity distribution and reduction.
summary_en.result: Optimal paving speed is identified to significantly reduce porosity levels.
summary_en.validation: Validation is based solely on simulation results without experimental confirmation.

papers.title: Biomechanical evaluation of mesh-based mandibular reconstruction plates and their implication for temporomandibular joint prosthesis
papers.abstract: • The present work compares mesh-based and conventional plates for mandible and TMJ reconstruction. • Experimental validation confirms FEA predictions within 7% stiffness deviation • The mesh-based Ti-6Al-4V plates improved load distribution over conventional solid plates. • Integration of mesh plate and TMJ prosthesis lowered fossa stress by up to 50%. Mandibular reconstruction involving the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) presents clinical challenges due to the need for both structural integrity and joint function. This study developed and biomechanically evaluated patient-specific mandibular reconstruction plates integrated with TMJ prostheses, focusing on mesh-based designs as an alternative to the conventional solid plate. The samples studied in this work included the conventional plate (CON-plate) and the mesh-based variants with relative densities (RD) from 0.2 to 1.0, fabricated using metal additive manufacturing. Finite element analysis (FEA) was validated with experimental compression tests, showing strong agreement in resulting stiffness, where both results differed by less than 7%. Under simulated masticatory loading, mesh-based plates demonstrated more uniform stress distribution, reducing peak stresses in both plates and screws by approximately 60%. In addition, an effective stress parameter was introduced to indicate mechanical efficiency relative to mass, demonstrating that the mesh-based plates achieve an improved stress–mass trade-off than the conventional design. Additionally, tribological testing showed that post-processing of Ti-6Al-4V pins reduced UHMWPE wear rate from 1.44 × 10 -4 mm 3 /Nm to 1.21 × 10 -4 mm 3 /Nm, highlighting the importance of surface finish. Integration of mesh-based plates also lowered von Mises stress and contact pressure in UHMWPE fossa components, indicating reduced wear potential. Overall, the mesh-based reconstruction plates present a promising strategy to enhance load transfer, minimize implant wear, and improve long-term outcomes for both mandibular reconstruction and TMJ prosthesis.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要关注下颌骨重建板的设计和力学性能，后处理仅作为磨损测试的附带提及，未深入研究后处理对Ti-6Al-4V疲劳和力学性能的影响。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not focus on the effect of post-processing on Ti-6Al-4V mechanical performance; it only briefly mentions post-processing of pins for wear reduction, and the main contribution is on implant design and load distribution.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发网格基下颌骨重建板以改善载荷分布和关节功能。
summary_zh.method: 通过有限元分析和压缩实验验证网格板与传统板的力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 网格板降低峰值应力约60%，并改善应力-质量权衡。
summary_zh.validation: 实验压缩测试验证FEA结果，刚度偏差小于7%。

summary_en.motivation: To develop patient-specific mesh-based mandibular reconstruction plates that improve load distribution and joint function compared to conventional solid plates.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis validated by experimental compression tests compared mesh-based plates of varying relative density to conventional plates under masticatory loading.
summary_en.result: Mesh-based plates reduced peak stresses in plates and screws by approximately 60% and achieved a better stress-mass trade-off, while integration with TMJ prosthesis lowered fossa stress by up to 50%.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression tests confirmed FEA predictions of stiffness within 7% deviation.
